content.title: About
content.content: Red unenriched dry raw rice is a whole‑grain product derived from rice varieties with a natural reddish hue. It has not been fortified with vitamins or minerals, preserving its original nutrient profile. The rice offers a mildly nutty flavor and a firm texture, suitable for a wide range of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red rice contains anthocyanins, natural pigments that give it its color and provide antioxidant benefits.
Raw dry rice can be stored for up to a year in a sealed container at room temperature.
In traditional Asian cuisine, red rice is often used in festive dishes and rituals as a symbol of prosperity.
Unenriched rice retains higher levels of natural minerals compared with fortified varieties.
Red rice requires a longer cooking time than white rice.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and phenolic compounds help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium is essential for muscle function, nerve signaling, and energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Red rice raises blood sugar more slowly, which can aid glucose control.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron is necessary for hemoglobin formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to rice.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Like other whole grains, rice can contain trace amounts of arsenic; a varied diet is recommended.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: High fiber content may cause discomfort for some people if consumed in large quantities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Red rice can be boiled, used in pilafs, soups, or salads. Before cooking, rinse the rice and soak for about 30 minutes to shorten cooking time. It works well as a base for vegetarian meals or as a side dish with meat and fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry raw rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and flavor loss.
